question: A developer has the same MCP server name "analytics" configured at the user scope, the project scope, and also started locally for the current session with different connection settings at each level. Per the documented scope hierarchy, which configuration does Claude actually use?
options: A) The project-level configuration, since project settings are considered the canonical source for a shared codebase
B) All three configurations merge together into a single combined connection for the "analytics" server
C) The local session-level configuration, since MCP servers override by name with local taking precedence over project and user
D) The user-level configuration, since user settings are meant to apply consistently across every project
correct_answers: C) The local session-level configuration, since MCP servers override by name with local taking precedence over project and user
explanations: Project scope sits between local and user in precedence; a local session-level configuration with the same server name overrides it, so project would not be the one used.
MCP servers do not merge configurations from multiple scopes when names collide; the documented behavior is a strict override based on precedence, not a combination.
Correct: MCP servers override by name following the precedence local > project > user, so the locally started session configuration for "analytics" wins over the other two.
User scope is the lowest precedence of the three in the documented hierarchy, so it is overridden whenever a project or local configuration with the same name exists.
